chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Salim who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Allah (Mighty and Majestic) Says: 'I am the best Associate. The one who associates someone else with Me in a deed he does, I will not Accept it except what was (done) for Me purely'.
ai.seo_question: What does Allah say about accepting deeds mixed with other partners?
ai.summary: This Qudsi hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the principle of *Ikhlas* (sincerity) by framing Allah as the ultimate 'Partner' in all human actions, thereby establishing that any deviation from exclusive devotion to Him renders the deed void. It serves as a foundational text in Shia theology for understanding how divine acceptance is contingent upon the purity of intention, distinguishing between mere ritual performance and spiritually valid worship.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Salim who said,

The one who associates someone else with Me<sup>azwj</sup> in a deed he does, I<sup>azwj</sup> will not Accept it except what was (done) for Me<sup>azwj</sup> purely’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn Salim who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, “I am the best associate (in a deal). Whoever associates others with Me in a deed that he has done, I will not accept it; I accept only what is purely for Me.’”
